status.label: Reproduce layout spacing reset
status.detail: Assigned investigation and supplied archives do not establish a fix; later reports include sleep and editor/runtime disagreement.

next_action.label: Trace persisted versus active spacing
next_action.reason: Distinguish layout identity migration from stale runtime state before changing persistence.

judgment.rationale: The report and follow-ups supply spacing settings, an edit/apply sequence and archives. The original assignment is not evidence of active implementation, and the later no-virtual-desktop case prevents treating desktop-ID migration as proven.
evidence: Priority Grid spacing disabled or set to zero later returns on PowerToys 0.57/0.58 across Windows 10/11.
The requested diagnostic archive was supplied; thirteen comments include a maintainer desktop-ID hypothesis, overlay/editor disagreement and sleep-related behavior.
AppliedLayouts.cpp loads/saves layouts and SyncVirtualDesktops can replace saved work-area desktop identifiers and copy layouts.
FancyZones recreates work areas on display/desktop changes; the shared symptom with 10379 is not sufficient to merge their different trigger sequences.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the supplied edit sequence and a desktop/sleep matrix to capture active layout ID and spacing alongside persisted settings; coordinate with the assigned maintainer.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete linked fix was found. A conditional layout-state correction can be investigated without asking for another generic archive.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve applied spacing through layout-state transitions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed: virtual-desktop/work-area identity reconciliation may select different saved layout settings, or a recreated work area may retain stale spacing despite correct saved settings. Later no-desktop reports prevent assuming only the first mechanism.
plan: Reproduce disabled/zero spacing and collect active work-area/layout IDs, runtime spacing and corresponding persisted applied/custom layout records before and after the trigger.
Compare virtual-desktop create/switch/delete, ordinary sleep/resume and editor save without desktop changes.

If identity reconciliation chooses a default or unrelated record, preserve the matched layout's explicit spacing through migration; if persisted settings remain correct, repair runtime reload instead.
Add focused tests for the confirmed transition and preserve existing per-desktop/per-monitor layout independence.
verification: Zero/disabled spacing survives desktop transitions and sleep/resume.
Editor display, persisted settings and actual zone overlay agree after apply.
Nonzero custom spacing and different layouts on separate desktops remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: Specific source transitions and supplied reports narrow the investigation, but differing later triggers and runtime/editor disagreement leave persistence versus reload unresolved.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones Priority Grid can restore spacing after it is disabled; the discussion broadens from desktop identity changes to sleep and stale active layout state.
known_information: The issue is assigned and includes thirteen comments and already-supplied diagnostics.
A maintainer suggested virtual-desktop identity handling, but no linked implementation proves coverage.
Later reports say the editor can still show spacing off and that the symptom can occur without virtual desktops.
inferences: The same visible reset can come from selecting a different saved layout or failing to refresh the active work area; they require different fixes.
issue_context.analysis: An assignee alone does not make this handled. Repeating the historical archive request is less useful than tracing persisted and runtime state through the supplied sequence.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report, all thirteen comments and obvious cross-references.
Read AppliedLayouts LoadData/SaveData and virtual-desktop reconciliation.
Checked FancyZones display-change and work-area initialization paths.

actions.label: Review spacing-state investigation
actions.description: Coordinate with the assigned maintainer before approving the conditional correction plan.

prerequisites: Use a current stable build and an instrumented development build; back up FancyZones settings.
Prepare Priority Grid with spacing disabled/zero, another layout with visible nonzero spacing, and two virtual desktops.
steps: Apply zero-spacing Priority Grid using the public edit sequence and compare editor, overlay and persisted records.
Switch/create/delete virtual desktops and repeat overlay checks without editing settings.
Repeat sleep/resume with a single desktop, then with multiple desktops.
Record active layout/work-area identity and saved spacing at the first divergence; restart FancyZones to distinguish stale runtime state.
reproduce.expected_result: The explicit spacing choice stays consistent between the editor, saved layout and actual overlay through each transition.
